sectionTypes.title: Section Type 0 elements
sectionTypes.summary:
Section Type 0 is used for indicating idle or guard periods from O-DU to
O-RU; see Table 7.4.2‑1

- Common Header Fields:

- **dataDirection** (data direction (gNB Tx/Rx)) field: 1 bit**.**

- **payloadVersion** (payload version) field: 3 bits:

- value = 1 shall be set (1st protocol version for payload
  and time reference format).

- **filterIndex** (filter index) field: 4 bits.

- **frameId** (frame identifier) field: 8 bits.

- **subframeId** (subframe identifier) field: 4 bits.

- **slotId** (slot identifier) field: 6 bits.

- **startSymbolId** (start symbol id) field: 6 bits.

sectionTypes.title: Section Type 1 elements
sectionTypes.summary:
Section Type 1 is used for most of the Downlink and Uplink radio
channels - some channels especially PRACH and mixed-numerology channels
may need more information elements contained in other Section Types.
However, if Section Type 1 is used for PRACH channel, it should be
processed in the same manner as a non-PRACH channel is processed in
O-RU; see Table 7.4.3‑1

- Common Header Fields:

- **dataDirection** (data direction (gNB Tx/Rx)) field: 1 bit**.**

- **payloadVersion** (payload version) field: 3 bits:

- value = 1 shall be set (1st protocol version for payload
  and time reference format).

sectionTypes.title: Section Type 3 elements
sectionTypes.summary:
Section Type 3 is used for PRACH and mixed-numerology channels; see
Table 7.4.5‑1:

- Common Header Fields:

- **dataDirection** (data direction (gNB Tx/Rx)) field: 1 bit**.**

- **payloadVersion** (payload version) field: 3 bits:

- value = 1 shall be set (1st protocol version for payload
  and time reference format).

- **filterIndex** (filter index) field: 4 bits.

- **frameId** (frame identifier) field: 8 bits.

- **subframeId** (subframe identifier) field: 4 bits.

- **slotId** (slot identifier) field: 6 bits.

- **startSymbolId** (start symbol identifier) field: 6 bits.

sectionTypes.title: Section Type 4 elements
sectionTypes.summary:
Section Type 4 (Slot level configuration); see Table 7.4.6‑1, Table
7.4.6-2:

- Common Header Fields:

- **dataDirection** (data direction (gNB Tx/Rx)) field: 1 bit**.**

- **payloadVersion** (payload version) field: 3 bits:

- value = 1 shall be set (1st protocol version for payload
  and time reference format).

- **scs** (filter index) field: 4 bits.

- **frameId** (frame identifier) field: 8 bits.

- **subframeId** (subframe identifier) field: 4 bits.

- **slotId** (slot identifier) field: 6 bits.

- **startSymbolId** (start symbol identifier) field: 6 bits.

sectionTypes.title: Section Type 5 elements
sectionTypes.summary:
Section Type 5 is used for UE scheduling information; see Table 7.4.7‑1:

- Common Header Fields:

- **dataDirection** (data direction (gNB Tx/Rx)) field: 1 bit**.**

- **payloadVersion** (payload version) field: 3 bits:

- value = 1 shall be set (1st protocol version for payload
  and time reference format).

- **filterIndex** (filter index) field: 4 bits.

- **frameId** (frame identifier) field: 8 bits.

- **subframeId** (subframe identifier) field: 4 bits.

- **slotId** (slot identifier) field: 6 bits.

- **startSymbolId** (start symbol identifier) field: 6 bits.

sectionTypes.title: Section Type 6 elements
sectionTypes.summary:
Section Type 6 is used for sending channel information for a specific
ueId; see Table 7.4.8‑1:

- Common Header Fields:

- **dataDirection** (data direction (gNB Tx/Rx)) field: 1 bit**.**

- **payloadVersion** (payload version) field: 3 bits:

- value = 1 shall be set (1st protocol version for payload
  and time reference format).

- **filterIndex** (filter index) field: 4 bits.

- **frameId** (frame identifier) field: 8 bits.

- **subframeId** (subframe identifier) field: 4 bits.

- **slotId** (slot identifier) field: 6 bits.

- **startSymbolId** (start symbol identifier) field: 6 bits.

sectionTypes.title: Section Type 7 elements
sectionTypes.summary:
Section Type 7 is used to support LAA; see Table 7.4.9‑1:

- Common Header Fields:

- dataDirection (data direction (gNB Tx/Rx)) field: 1 bit.

- value = 1 shall be set

- **payloadVersion** (payload version) field: 3 bits:

- value = 1 shall be set (1st protocol version for payload
  and time reference format).

- **reserved** (reserved for future use) field: 4 bits.

- **frameId** (frame identifier) field: 8 bits.

- **subframeId** (subframe identifier) field: 4 bits.

- **slotId** (slot identifier) field: 6 bits.

- **reserved** (reserved for future use) field: 14 bits.

sectionTypes.title: Section Type 8 elements
sectionTypes.summary:
Section Type 8 is used for sending ACK/NACK feedbacks from the O-RU to
the O-DU; see Table 7.4.10‑1:

- Common Header Fields

- **dataDirection** (data direction (gNB Tx/Rx)) field: 1 bit.

- **payloadVersion** (payload version) field: 3 bits

- value = 1 shall be set (1st protocol version for payload
  and time reference format)

- **scs** (sub-carrier spacing) field: 4 bits

- **frameId** (frame identifier) field: 8 bits

- **subframeId** (subframe identifier) field: 4 bits

- **slotId** (slot identifier) field: 6 bits

- **symbolId** (symbolId identifier) field: 6 bits

sectionTypes.title: Section Type 10 elements
sectionTypes.summary:
Section Type 10 is used for sending RRM measurement reports from O-RU to
O-DU; see Table 7.4.12-1:

- Common Header Fields:

- **dataDirection** (data direction (gNB Tx/Rx)) field: 1 bit**.**

- value = 0 (uplink) shall be used

- **payloadVersion** (payload version) field: 3 bits:

- value = 1 shall be set (1st protocol version for payload
  and time reference format).

- **reserved** (reserved for future use) field: 4 bits**.**

- **frameId** (frame identifier) field: 8 bits.

- **subframeId** (subframe identifier) field: 4 bits.

- **slotId** (slot identifier) field: 6 bits.

sectionTypes.title: Section Type 11 elements
sectionTypes.summary:
Section Type 11 is sent from O-DU to O-RU to request RRM measurements.
It supports a command to request IpN for unallocated PRBs, see table
7.4.13-1.

- Common Header Fields:

- **dataDirection** (data direction (gNB Tx/Rx)) field: 1 bit**.**

- value = 0 (uplink) shall be used

- **payloadVersion** (payload version) field: 3 bits:

- value = 1 shall be set (1st protocol version for payload
  and time reference format).

- **reserved** (reserved for future use) field: 4 bits.

- **frameId** (frame identifier) field: 8 bits.

- **subframeId** (subframe identifier) field: 4 bits.

sectionExtensions.title: Beamforming weights
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.1.1 Overview

Section Extension 1 applies to the sending of beamforming weights from
the O-DU to the O-RU. When Section Extension 1 is present in a section
description, O-RU shall associate the set of beamforming weights
conveyed in Section Extension 1 with the beamId conveyed in the section
description. In subsequent C-Plane messages, the same beamId can be
invoked without sending the beamforming weights again.

NOTE: This allows downloaded weights to have "persistence" which saves
DL throughput by not requiring sending of weights multiple times.

sectionExtensions.title: DL precoding parameters
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.3.1 Overview

Section Extension 3 applies only to Category B O-RU and to Section Types
1 and 3. Section Extension 3 may be used only for precoding schemes
Transmit Diversity and Spatial Multiplexing with Large Delay CDD; for
other LTE transmission modes and for NR, if there is precoding in the DL
processing chain, precoding shall be included in the beamforming
operation (that is, encoded in the beamforming weights).

[Table 7.7.3.1‑1](#tab_7_7_3_1_SE3_Data_Format_First_Layer) shows the
format of Section Extension 3 for the first data layer.

sectionExtensions.summary: #### 7.7.5.1 Overview

sectionExtensions.title: Non-contiguous PRB allocation in time and frequency domain
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.6.1 Overview

Section Extension 6 applies to Section Types 1, 3, 5, 10, and 11.

Section Extension 6 enables allocation of non-contiguous sets of PRBs
(Resource Block Groups, or RBGs) in frequency and time domain. This
reduces the C-Plane overhead when users or channels are allocated with
non-contiguous sets of PRBs in time and frequency.

If Section Extension 6 is present in a section description, then the
following requirements apply:

sectionExtensions.title: eAxC mask
sectionExtensions.summary: #### 7.7.7.1 Overview

sectionExtensions.title: Regularization factor
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.8.1 Overview

This Section Extension is used for conveying value of regularization
factor used for generating multi-user beamforming weight for the
scheduled UEs in a slot. Regularization factor is the noise variance
used in, for example, MMSE (Minimum Mean Square Error) and RZF
(Regularized Zero-Forcing) computation of multi-user beamforming
weights. The intended use case applies to Section Type 5 for sending
regularization factor. See Annex J for further description of the
regularization factor's use in uplink and downlink.

sectionExtensions.title: Group configuration of multiple ports
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.10.1 Overview

This Section Extension applies to Section Types 1, 3 and 5. In most
cases, C-Plane section information for the multiple ports (i.e. layers
or Tx/Rx paths) can be the same except beam IDs or UE IDs. When multiple
ports share common section information within an O-RU, the C-Plane
sections to be sent via corresponding ports are merged into one C-Plane
section via a representative port using this Section Extension. The
formatting of this Section Extension is determined by the value of
beamGroupType parameter.

sectionExtensions.title: Flexible beamforming weights
sectionExtensions.summary: #### 7.7.11.1 Overview

sectionExtensions.title: Non-contiguous PRB allocation with frequency ranges
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.12.1 Overview

Section Extension 12 applies to Section Types 1, 3, 5, 10 and 11. It
cannot be used with Section Extension 6 in the same section description.

sectionExtensions.title: PRB allocation with frequency hopping
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.13.1 Overview

Section Extension 13 applies only to Section Types 1, 3 and 5.

Section Extension 13 allows to describe two or more PRB allocations
starting at different symbols and different PRB. It is intended to be
used for allocations with intra-slot frequency hopping. This Section
Extension reduces the C-Plane overhead when users or channels are
allocated with intra-slot frequency hopping. This extension is more
space-efficient than the use of several section descriptions. Structure
of Section Extension 13 is presented in [Table
7.7.13.1‑1](#tab_7_7_13_1_SE13).

sectionExtensions.title: Nulling layer information for ueId based beamforming
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.14.1 Overview

This Section Extension applies to Section Type 5. This enables the O-DU
to provide layer-by-layer indication, which denotes that the
corresponding ueId is for nulling-layer indication.

Section Extension 14 shall follow the formatting defined in Table
[7.7.14.1‑1](#tab_7_SE14).

sectionExtensions.summary:

sectionExtensions.title: Indication of user port group
sectionExtensions.summary: #### 7.7.17.1 Overview

sectionExtensions.title: Uplink transmission management
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.18.1 Introduction

This Section Extension applies to sending of transmission windows
information for management of the uplink user data transmission from the
O-RU. With the two parameters included in this Section Extension the
O-RU shall transmit the corresponding user data within that time window.
The data shall either be sent in normal transmission mode or be
uniformly distributed in time depending on value of toT parameter. This
Section Extension applies to Section Types 1, 3, and 5. The format of
Section Extension 18 is specified in [Table 7.7.18.1‑1](#_Ref97937858)

sectionExtensions.title: Compact beamforming information for multiple port
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.19.1 Overview

This Section Extension applies to Section Types 1 and 3. This Section
Extension shall be used for sending compact beamforming information for
multiple antenna ports (the term 'port' used henceforth in context of
this Section Extension refers to logical antenna port). The optional
"little endian byte order" is applied to bfwI/bfwQ fields if chosen via
M-Plane. Refer to Annex D.2 for details of little endian byte order.
CSI-RS channel will benefit the most from using this extension,
considering large number of CSI-RS ports and multiple CSI resource sets.

sectionExtensions.title: Dedicated puncturing
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.20.1 Overview

This Section Extension can be used with Section Types 1, 3, 5, 10, and
11. This extension specifies a puncturing pattern to be applied to the
section description and optionally to sections following the section
description in the same C-Plane message. This extension contains a
common header with the number of puncturing patterns, followed by
puncSymbolMask, PRB ranges, puncReMask and optionally RBG mask fields
for each puncturing pattern.

sectionExtensions.title: Variable PRB group size for channel information
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.21.1 Overview

This Section Extension may be sent with Section Type 5 or Section Type
6. It enables the O-DU to send channel information with dynamic PRB
group size that can match the channel variation in the frequency domain
and reduce the fronthaul traffic. SE 21 is applicable for CIBF.

sectionExtensions.title: ACK/NACK request
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.22.1 Overview

Section Extension 22 enables the O-DU to request ACK/NACK feedback using
Section Type 8 C-Plane message for a section description. SE 22 can be
used with all Section Types that support Section Extensions and are sent
from O-DU to O-RU. SE 22 can be used with all Section Extensions sent
from O-DU to O-RU. Section Extension 22 shall follow the format defined
in Table [7.7.22.1-1](#tab_SE22_acknackreqid).

sectionExtensions.title: Arbitrary symbol pattern modulation compression parameters
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.23.1 Overview

This Section Extension enables specifying multiple sets of
'mcScaleReMask, csf and mcScaleOffset' values for one or more
'SymPrbPatterns'. The term 'SymPrbPattern' is used to specify set of
PRBs that can span an entire PRB range (specified using prbPattern) and
multiple symbols (specified using symMask). In context of this Section
Extension the term SymPrbPattern is defined for each mode of operation:

- for PRB-MASK mode SymPrbPattern is one set of parameters symMask and
  prbPattern,

sectionExtensions.title: PUSCH DMRS configuration
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.24.1 Overview

The Section Extension 24 is used with Section Type 5 to convey PUSCH
DMRS configuration used for DMRS-BF-EQ and DMRS-BF-NEQ beamforming
methods. The principles of providing DMRS configuration in Section
Type 5 are specified in clause 12.6.1.3.1.

sectionExtensions.title: Symbol reordering for DMRS-BF
sectionExtensions.summary: #### 7.7.25.1 Overview

sectionExtensions.title: Frequency offset feedback
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.26.1 Overview

This Section Extension is used with Section Type 5 to deliver the UE
frequency offset from the O-DU to the O-RU and is valid only when
dataDirection bit = 0 and when SE 24 is present and SE 24 shall precede
SE 26. The O-RU derives frequency offset value for channel estimation
using the received value and the estimated value. The format of SE 26 is
defined in Table 7.7.26.1-1.

sectionExtensions.title: O-DU controlled dimensionality reduction
sectionExtensions.summary: #### 7.7.27.1 Overview

sectionExtensions.title: O-DU controlled frequency resolution for SINR reporting
sectionExtensions.summary: #### 7.7.28.1 Overview

sectionExtensions.title: Cyclic delay adjustment
sectionExtensions.summary: #### 7.7.29.1 Overview

sectionExtensions.title: PUSCH repetition indication
sectionExtensions.summary:
#### 7.7.30.1 Overview

Section Extension 30 applies to Section Type 5 to provide PUSCH
repetition indications for scheduled PUSCH transmissions. Section
Extension 30 is valid only when dataDirection bit = 0. O-RU supporting
PUSCH repetition indication may optimize its PUSCH reception for
repeated transmissions if it receives PUSCH repetition indication from
O-DU. In the present document, SE 30 is specified to support only
single-layer PUSCH repetition per UE.
